content: Mifepristone interacts with various drugs by influencing the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, leading to changes in drug levels and effects. Below are the detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Ribociclib: Mifepristone increases ribociclib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely if used together. 2. Rifabutin: Rifabutin decreases mifepristone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 3. Rifampin: Rifampin reduces mifepristone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid co-administration if possible. 4. Rifapentine: Rifapentine decreases mifepristone levels through CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid co-administration. 5. Rimegepant: Mifepristone increases rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Riociguat: Mifepristone increases riociguat levels by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor for hypotension and adjust the dose if necessary. 7. Ripretinib: Mifepristone increases ripretinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Risperidone: Both mifepristone and risperidone prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 9. Ritonavir: Ritonavir increases mifepristone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing’s syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 10. Rivaroxaban: Mifepristone increases rivaroxaban levels and toxicity by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may increase the risk of bleeding. Avoid or modify therapy and monitor closely. 11. Roflumilast (topical): Mifepristone increases roflumilast levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Romidepsin: Mifepristone increases romidepsin levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely. 13. Rosiglitazone: Mifepristone increases rosiglitazone levels by inhibiting CYP2C8/2C9. Use the smallest recommended doses and monitor closely. 14. Rosuvastatin: Mifepristone increases rosuvastatin toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely. 15. Rucaparib: Rucaparib increases mifepristone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 16. Ruxolitinib: Mifepristone increases ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 17. Sacubitril/Valsartan: Mifepristone increases sacubitril/valsartan levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Salmeterol: Mifepristone increases salmeterol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Saxagliptin: Mifepristone increases saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 20. Segesterone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Mifepristone decreases the effects of these contraceptives through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use a backup contraceptive method and monitor closely. 21. Seladelpar: Mifepristone increases seladelpar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution, especially in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers. Monitor closely. 22. Selegiline: Mifepristone increases selegiline levels by inhibiting CYP2C8/2C9/2B6. Use the smallest recommended doses and monitor closely. 23. Selexipag: Mifepristone increases selexipag levels by reducing its metabolism. Reduce the selexipag dose to once daily if co-administered with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 24. Selpercatinib: Mifepristone increases selpercatinib levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Reduce selpercatinib dosage if co-administration is necessary. Monitor ECGs for QT prolongation. 25. Selumetinib: Mifepristone increases selumetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 26. Sertraline: Both mifepristone and sertraline prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 27. Sevoflurane: Both mifepristone and sevoflurane prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 28. Sildenafil: Mifepristone increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 29. Simvastatin: Mifepristone increases simvastatin levels and toxicity. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy. 30. Siponimod: Mifepristone increases siponimod levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Sirolimus: Mifepristone increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 32. Sitagliptin: Mifepristone increases sitagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP2C8/2C9. Use the smallest recommended doses and monitor closely. 33. Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Mifepristone increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Solifenacin: Mifepristone increases solifenacin levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 35. Sonidegib: Mifepristone increases sonidegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Sorafenib: Mifepristone increases sorafenib levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 37. Sotalol: Both mifepristone and sotalol prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 38. Sparsentan: Mifepristone and sparsentan increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 39. St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases mifepristone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended. 40. Stiripentol: Mifepristone increases stiripentol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor closely. 41. Sufentanil: Mifepristone increases sufentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the sufentanil dose and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 42. Sunitinib: Mifepristone increases sunitinib levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 43. Suvorexant: Mifepristone increases suvorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 44. Tacrolimus: Mifepristone increases tacrolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 45. Tadalafil: Mifepristone increases tadalafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Tamoxifen: Mifepristone decreases tamoxifen effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Tamsulosin: Mifepristone increases tamsulosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Tasimetostat: Mifepristone increases tasimetostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 49. Tecovirimat: Tecovirimat decreases mifepristone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Telavancin: Both mifepristone and telavancin prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 51. Temsirolimus: Mifepristone increases temsirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Allow a one-week period after discontinuing mifepristone before increasing the temsirolimus dose. 52. Terbinafine: Mifepristone increases terbinafine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Tetrabenazine: Both mifepristone and tetrabenazine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 54. Tezacaftor: Mifepristone increases tezacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 55. Thioridazine: Both mifepristone and thioridazine prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 56. Thiothixene: Both mifepristone and thiothixene prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 57. Tiagabine: Mifepristone increases tiagabine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 58. Ticagrelor: Mifepristone increases ticagrelor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Tinidazole: Mifepristone increases tinidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Tinzaparin: Mifepristone increases the risk of excessive bleeding in patients on anticoagulant therapy. Co-administration is contraindicated. 61. Tipranavir: Mifepristone increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 62. Tisotumab Vedotin: Mifepristone increases tisotumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Tofacitinib: Mifepristone increases tofacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the tofacitinib dose if co-administered. 64. Tolterodine: Mifepristone increases tolterodine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the tolterodine dose and monitor for QT prolongation. 65. Tolvaptan: Mifepristone increases tolvaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 66. Toremifene: Mifepristone increases toremifene levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 67. Tovorafenib: Mifepristone increases tovorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP2C8 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 68. Trabectedin: Mifepristone increases trabectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 69. Tramadol: Mifepristone increases tramadol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Trazodone: Mifepristone increases trazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 71. Treprostinil: Mifepristone increases treprostinil levels by inhibiting CYP2C8/2C9. Use the smallest recommended doses and monitor closely. 72. Tretinoin: Mifepristone increases tretinoin levels by inhibiting CYP2C8/2C9. Use the smallest recommended doses and monitor closely. 73. Triamcinolone Acetonide (Injectable): Mifepristone is contraindicated in patients on long-term corticosteroid therapy. 74. Triazolam: Mifepristone increases triazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 75. Triclabendazole: Both mifepristone and triclabendazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 76. Trimipramine: Mifepristone increases trimipramine levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 77. Triptorelin: Triptorelin increases mifepristone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 78. Tucatinib: Mifepristone increases tucatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 79. Ubrogepant: Mifepristone increases ubrogepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 80. Ulipristal: Mifepristone increases ulipristal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 81. Umeclidinium Bromide/Vilanterol (Inhaled): Mifepristone increases umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 82. Upadacitinib: Mifepristone increases upadacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 83. Valbenazine: Both mifepristone and valbenazine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 84. Valsartan: Mifepristone increases valsartan levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 85. Vamorolone: Mifepristone increases vamorolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of vamorolone and monitor closely. 86. Vandetanib: Mifepristone increases vandetanib levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 87. Vardenafil: Mifepristone increases vardenafil levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 88. Velpatasvir: Mifepristone increases velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 89. Vemurafenib: Mifepristone increases vemurafenib levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 90. Venetoclax: Mifepristone increases venetoclax levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 91. Venlafaxine: Mifepristone increases venlafaxine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 92. Verapamil: Mifepristone increases verapamil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 93. Vilanterol/Fluticasone Furoate (Inhaled): Mifepristone increases vilanterol/fluticasone furoate levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 94. Vilazodone: Mifepristone increases vilazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the vilazodone dose if intolerable adverse effects occur. 95. Vinblastine: Mifepristone increases vinblastine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 96. Vincristine: Mifepristone increases vincristine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 97. Vincristine (Liposomal): Mifepristone increases vincristine liposomal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. These interactions highlight the importance of careful monitoring and dose adjustments when mifepristone is co-administered with other medications.
